After invert_node_selection the selection flips: A, C, D, and F are selected and B and E are plain." width="100%"} Replaces the node selection with its complement: every currently selected node becomes unselected and every unselected node becomes selected. With no nodes selected, the result is that all nodes are selected. Inverting turns any selection rule into its negation without having to write a second rule, which is useful for: - keeping a subset rather than removing it, e.g., select the nodes to keep, invert, then `delete_nodes_ws()` - selecting "everything except" a neighborhood, community, or set of hubs - selecting all nodes (invert an empty selection) as input to a `*_ws` method Any edge selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both; to invert an edge selection, use `invert_edge_selection()`. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 10-node path, the two endpoints have degree `1` while every other node has degree `2`. Selecting the endpoints and then inverting leaves the 8 middle nodes selected instead: ::: {#9831da7d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_path_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(max_degree=1) .invert_node_selection() ) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 8 ``` ::: ::: Inverting a neighborhood selects everything outside it. Here the nodes more than one hop away from "A" are selected and then removed, keeping only the ego network of "A": ::: {#18b42d7b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) .select_nodes_in_neighborhood("A", k=1) .invert_node_selection() .delete_nodes_ws() ) graph.get_node_df().select("id", "label") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
